# AFTER HOURS

A complete, playable first-person browser prototype based on the supplied Eli/Mara story. One connected school block carries the full narrative arc, including the original final voicemail and ending. Expect approximately 20–35 minutes including retries, depending on exploration and reading.

## Run

```sh
cd after-hours
npm start
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:4173** in a desktop browser with WebGL enabled. Use a keyboard and mouse; headphones help locate footsteps and ringing phones. Click **Enter the school** to enable audio and mouse capture. There is **no installation of npm dependencies** and no external asset/CDN request during play: Three.js is vendored with its license. Node 16+ runs the server; Node 20+ is recommended and required for the supplied test commands. An alternative without Node is `python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1` from this folder.

On macOS, `Start After Hours.command` starts the local server. The browser is opened separately. Keep the terminal running while playing. `PORT=4180 npm start` uses another port if 4173 is occupied. Serve the folder over HTTP; opening `index.html` directly will block ES modules in most browsers.

## Controls

| Input                            | Action                                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WASD                             | Walk                                                                    |
| Mouse                            | Look                                                                    |
| Shift                            | Sprint (limited breath); louder and easier to hear                      |
| C / left Ctrl (hold)             | Crouch; quieter and less visible                                        |
| E                                | Use the object under the reticle; leave a hiding place; put down a note |
| B                                | Replace flashlight battery (+70%); requires a spare                     |
| Tab                              | Show/hide carried keys and tools                                        |
| F2                               | Open the paused cheat panel                                             |
| R                                | Retry after capture                                                     |
| F                                | Toggle flashlight                                                       |
| Space                            | Jump; skip a brief story shot while it is playing                       |
| Q                                | Advance a subtitle after its short reading period                       |
| E (tap repeatedly while grabbed) | Break free from a room monster                                          |
| Esc                              | Pause / resume; close a note                                            |
| Arrow keys                       | Alternate camera control                                                |
| Hold mouse button + drag         | Look when the browser denies pointer lock                               |

The objective names the room or prop to find. Choose Story, Easy, Normal, Hard, or Nightmare before entering. Normal gives 5.5 seconds of sprint reserve, a 4.1 m/s Teacher chase and 20-second searches; Hard uses 4.5 seconds, 4.45 m/s and 24-second searches. Each preset relocates all six keys/tools into a fixed, solvable layout. Story mode keeps the story/scares but prevents Teacher captures; room monsters remain lethal. Walk/crouch between bursts and listen for her retreat. Reach Classroom 08 unseen to finish the first encounter; waiting in a hiding place never completes it. In the east wing, hold E for 1.35 seconds to force the warped door, close the classroom corridor door to break sight before hiding, then reach the west staff records after pursuit ends. You cannot pick up notes while being chased or while she is within six metres. Safe inspection pauses the game.

A witnessed locker or desk entry is unsafe: the Teacher approaches, rattles the door, and catches you after a short check unless you leave. Crouching, switching off the torch, real walls and blind hiding help. Capture has a close Teacher jumpscare and an explicit failure screen. Press **R** or **Try again** to restart the encounter with full breath; dialogue preceding the encounter is not repeated. Death is possible and expected while learning, but neither encounter requires an unavoidable death. There is no combat. The Teacher uses collision-aware movement throughout pursuit.

Progress, inventory, used supplies, unlocked doors, repaired power, selected preset, and resource levels are saved at story beats and successful item actions in this browser. Retry restores collected keys/tools, full stamina, and minimum reserves of 30% flashlight / 55% sanity so repeated attempts cannot strand you without light. Older saves reconstruct completed prerequisites. **Continue from checkpoint** restores the appropriate environment, character placement and doors. **Restore checkpoint** in the pause menu recovers from being lost or stuck. Capture fades to the current checkpoint without a gore/death scene. Restarting after the ending starts the story again. Browser storage may be unavailable in strict private-browsing configurations; manual recovery still uses the current stage.

## What is built

- A real 3D school: lobby, long corridors, classrooms, office, records room, maintenance passage, gym and an exterior entrance. Collision follows walls and actual door openings. Labels, lockers, dirty tiled floors, fluorescent fixtures, rain-streaked windows, puddles, noticeboards, desks, CRT, cassette deck, telephone and electrical cabinets ground it in an ordinary school.
- First-person walking, running, crouching, mouse look, footsteps, a visible hand gripping a modeled metal flashlight, a beam emitted from the torch, and line-of-sight interaction.
- Shared interactions for doors, lockers, drawers, notes, phones, cassette players, switches, story objects and hiding locations. A handmade beaded bracelet becomes visible when Mara's locker opens.
- Data-driven, once-only story triggers with serialized effects and cancellation when a checkpoint is restored. Dialogue, positional sound, objectives, lighting, room states, enemy events, fades and companion sequences share the dispatcher.
- Ruined, normal, burned, distorted and memory palettes; room-specific variants; warm/cold lighting; props that disappear in memories; lights dying behind the player; optical corridor stretching; the source's boundary during the playable abandonment.
- Recorded positional concrete/wood footsteps, heavy Teacher steps, doors/creaks, cloth, landing, metal/wood impacts and composed scare/collapse WAVs, alongside generated rain, hum, phone rings, chalk, alarms, breath, bell and sparse memory tones. Audio often precedes visual contact. All 57 spoken line assignments play automatically using 54 separate Seed Audio performances, plus a licensed recorded laugh, with distinct present and memory Eli, child Mara, older Mara and Mrs. Vale voices. Web Audio buffer playback, positional device filtering, pause/resume and cancellation keep dialogue reliable. The old OS voices and browser-speech fallback are removed. The v11 recordings replace the earlier Microsoft neural takes. They remain generated voices, with local 48kHz PCM playback and unchanged story wording.
- The Teacher's Patrol, Suspicious, Investigate, Search, Chase and Return states. Sight uses distance, facing angle, crouch visibility and walls. Hearing uses movement noise. Grid navigation respects dynamic door collision. Hiding breaks sight; fixed speed, advance cues and an initial grace period keep pursuits readable.
- Mara's older companion form follows collision-aware routes, reaches a latch through a small gap, stays at the entrance, and returns to her childhood form for the last classroom. Emotional dialogue generally leaves the camera and movement in the player's hands.
- Minimal title, pause, reading and ending UI, plus a live **Director / Tuning** panel.

Mara now uses a fully clothed authored female skinned GLB from Quaternius (CC0), with a coherent face and hands, adjusted navy clothing, removed backpack, smoothed skin normals, and independent idle/walk animation. Child scenes adjust stature and head proportions. Mrs. Vale now uses an independent clone of the authored human skeleton, formal blouse/collar, continuous skirt, wire spectacles and a readable staff badge. Her burnt form has charred surface shading, a ragged hem, blackened mouth, off-axis head, elongated stature, and authored idle/walk motion. The photograph and drawing are actual generated image assets, displayed on props and in the inspection view. Mara is a stylized authored model, Mrs. Vale is also a stylized authored rig, and voices are synthetic; full actor facial performances, a choreographed embrace, physical building destruction, a playable stairwell floor and full impossible-space topology remain production work. Its hugs use proximity and framing; collapse uses lighting and sound; the memory's hallway stretches optically. Replace these through the existing systems rather than adding new plot. See `assets/ASSET-PLAN.md`.

## Resources, locks, presets, and cheats

Three persistent HUD meters show sanity, stamina and flashlight charge. Sprint drains stamina; standing or walking restores it. The torch drains only while lit and visible; below 25% it develops intermittent dropouts, and at 0% its beam switches off. Batteries are small cylinders concealed inside searchable storage: collect with E, replace with B. Install the maintenance fuse using E at the marked fuse box. The repaired box becomes a reusable charger; returning to it is an exposure/route decision. Light and stillness help sanity, darkness and nearby pursuit erode it, and memories/time with Mara restore it. Low sanity introduces heartbeat and a cold peripheral vignette; it never forces an unavoidable death or steals camera control.

The gate chain is: reception locker key → Mara’s locker; office key → Classroom 04; key inside Classroom 04 drawers → Classroom 08; key inside Classroom 08 drawers → staff record; maintenance fuse → restored power and fire record; archive bolt cutters → either gym entrance. Search lockers and drawers in those rooms; objectives name the current requirement. Both gym entrances are locked so the maintenance route cannot bypass the tool puzzle. The existing warped chase door still uses hold E. Key/tool possession persists; installed fuses are consumed. Story props use separate supported footprints, and reticle hits take priority over nearby objects.

Edit `ITEMS` and `STORAGE` in `src/data/items.js` to add items and per-preset storage slots. `ITEM_LAYOUTS` is derived from those slots. Add a world target with `type:'pickup', item:'yourItem', id:'uniquePickup'`; give its lock target `requires:'yourItem'`. For physical doors also set `door.requires`. Keep each prerequisite on the accessible side of the lock and provide a reachable container approach. `InventorySystem` owns collection, unlocks, charging, snapshots and old-save hydration. Update `hydrateStage` when adding a new story gate. Expose depletion settings in `TUNING` and tune chase, supply counts, starting charge and movement reserve in `PRESETS`.

F2 (or Esc → Cheats) pauses play and offers cannot-be-caught, infinite stamina/sanity/flashlight, freeze Teacher, disable room ambushes, any key/tool, give all supplies, unlock doors, refill bars, safe room teleports, and a story checkpoint selector. Checkpoint jumps reconstruct completed prerequisites and cancel pending dialogue/camera sequences. Cheat switches reset on a new game. Giving items affects the saved inventory on the next item action/story checkpoint; toggle flags themselves are not persisted. Story mode and frozen-Teacher cheats still allow the first encounter’s safe-room progression.

Mara’s `voiceProfile:'mara-device'` routes intercom and voicemail through telephone bandwidth and restrained ring modulation; childhood groups use the unprocessed child voice. Device placement still uses positional HRTF. For a new device line set `voiceProfile` explicitly; a `mara-child` manifest entry uses the bundled child performance with no robotic processing. These are synthetic performances, not a recorded child actor. Replace their WAVs with directed actor recordings for final performances.

## Story triggers and new sequences

`STAGES` gives each stage its chapter, objective, safe checkpoint position, environment and companion/enemy flags. `BEATS` binds an event to a stage, then performs ordered effects. Example from the current story:

```js
{
  id: 'bracelet', stage: 'locker', event: 'interact', target: 'bracelet',
  effects: [
    { type: 'audio', name: 'door' },
    { type: 'dialogue', id: 'intercom' },
    { type: 'door', id: 'exit', open: false },
    { type: 'stage', stage: 'drawing' }
  ]
}
```

An interaction calls `story.signal('interact', prop.id)`. A spatial check calls `story.signal('location', 'namedRegion')`. Timed encounters and hiding call the same dispatcher. `TriggerSystem` also supports `when(context, event)` conditions. Every beat needs a unique ID. Effects run in order, await dialogue/waits, and stop when the checkpoint generation changes. The player can move during effects unless a reader, brief seating pose, or camera sequence is active. Duplicate uses never double-advance the story.

To add a sequence **within the existing story**, add its stage and checkpoint to `STAGES`, add a beat in `BEATS`, and add a region check in `StorySystem.update` or a target in the world. Link it with `{type:'stage', stage:'nextStage'}`. Extend the actions dictionary in `StorySystem` when a new reusable effect is needed. Current effects include `dialogue`, `environment`, `audio`, `objective`, `lighting`, `wait`, `stage`, `mara`, `hideMara`, `teacher`, `teleport`, `read`, `fade`, `silhouette`, `door`, `sunrise`, `embrace`, `companionGap`, `sit`, `exterior` and `end`.

`lighting` accepts `minZ`, `maxZ`, `multiplier`, optional numeric `color`, and `behind`. `wait` uses game-aware timing: it stops counting during pause and reading. Keep each checkpoint reachable and restore the correct doors, actors and environment in `StorySystem.start`.

## Dialogue and objectives

Add an array under a unique key in `src/data/dialogue.js`:

```js
existingLine: [
  {
    speaker: "MARA",
    text: "I knew you’d come back.",
    duration: 6,
    audio: "assets/audio/mara-reunion.wav",
  },
];
```

Trigger it with `{type:'dialogue', id:'existingLine'}`. The `VOICES` manifest automatically assigns bundled clips to existing lines. A new line can provide `audio` directly or add a manifest entry. If a clip is missing, the line remains subtitled without a robotic voice fallback. Spoken dialogue is on by default and can be muted in the pause menu. Set `duration` to the actual performance length, including pauses. Speaker names and long silences are intentional. Dialogue remains in source order; replace clips without changing its words. Set a stage's `objective` string to create an objective automatically, or use `{type:'objective', id:'existingGoal', text:'Return to Classroom 04 together.'}` inside a sequence. `ObjectiveSystem` displays it without a quest log or waypoints.

## The Teacher and tuning

Use **Esc → Director / Tuning** to adjust walking/sprint/crouch speed, interaction distance, flashlight cone/reach/brightness, vision/hearing, chase/patrol speed, search duration, sound volume, dialogue timing, trigger timing and environment fades. Values persist locally; use **Restore default values** to reset. Edit `DEFAULTS` for project-wide defaults. Camera sensitivity, eye height, sight angle, suspicion time, footstep cadence and renderer pixel ratio are also editable there.

`TeacherAI.activate(x,z)` starts a patrol. Set `patrol` waypoints and `home` in `teacher.js`, or configure them when activating a scene. `change('Investigate', position)` sends her toward a noise, `change('Chase', position)` starts an explicit pursuit, and `deactivate()` protects a story scene. The first encounter grants 1.8 seconds of grace after the arrival shot; the east-wing chase starts behind the player with an audible approach and 0.6 seconds of initial grace. Restored checkpoints grant 1.8 seconds. Chase continues for three seconds after sight breaks and then becomes a 24-second search. Set `sprintCapacity`, `sprintRecovery`, `lostSightDuration`, `hideCheckDuration`, and `encounterGrace` in config.js to tune this. Keep chase speed slightly below sprint speed. Investigation times out if its target is unreachable. Routes align at grid centres before corners to avoid sticking against lockers.

## New props and hiding places

World targets share `{id,label,mesh,type,position,enabled}`. `type` dispatches behaviour in `InteractionSystem.use`; `note` references `NOTES`, and a door references `{hinge,leaf,obstacle,open}`. Focus requires distance, a camera cone and unblocked sight. Target surfaces inside their own cabinet/table are excluded from obstruction checks so they remain usable.

A locker or desk hiding target adds:

```js
{
  id: 'hideNew', type: 'hide', label: 'Hide under desk',
  mesh, position: mesh.position.clone(), enabled: true,
  hide: { x: safeX, z: safeZ, y: 0.56, yaw: Math.PI }
}
```

Register it in `world.interactables` and `world.hideSpots`. Choose a camera location under the desk or inside the locker, and a reachable exterior approach. Entering saves the prior player position, silences movement and turns off the light; E returns to that safe exterior position. The Teacher cannot directly see a hidden player, but `noticeHide(target)` remembers an entry she witnessed and searches that location. Call it before changing the player to hidden. Choose hiding approaches with nearby solid walls so the player can break sight first. Locker hiding also uses a slatted view overlay. Use unique target IDs when adding multiple props.

## Present/memory environment variants

`EnvironmentSystem.register(mesh, role, room, variants)` makes an object state-aware. `PALETTES` defines colors, ambience and fog for `ruined`, `normal`, `burned`, `distorted` and `memory`. Roles include walls, trim, floors, ceilings, desks and lockers. The world helpers register these automatically.

```js
env.register(brokenTile, "debris", "classroom", {
  ruined: { visible: true },
  memory: { visible: false },
  normal: { visible: false },
});
env.set("memory", "classroom"); // just this room
env.set("burned"); // whole school
```

A variant can set `visible` and `scale`. For a completely different model, register both normal and ruined meshes with complementary visibility variants. Register props as separate components; avoid rebuilding a room for every memory. Door collision changes through `world.openDoor`, not a cosmetic visibility swap. Keep collision topology stable during fades unless the sequence explicitly relocates the player to a verified checkpoint.

## Narrative fidelity

The source is preserved unchanged in `assets/STORY-SOURCE.txt`; spoken words are checked against it with the user-approved reunion and clarity revisions listed in `ADAPTATIONS.md`. Artifacts turn its existing facts into inspectable text. Spatial labels, room placement and objective instructions are adaptation scaffolding. The cause stays unexplained beyond the electrical fault and embedded final moments; the user-requested room shadows add gameplay hazards without factions, experiments or explanations. The exit is never an alternate ending. Eli returns, Mara absolves him, they walk inward together, the bell becomes normal, nobody emerges, and the final voicemail ends with **“I am.”**

The supplied source contains continuity conflicts: Eli is introduced as 17 eight years after Mara's death at nine, while the fire memory also calls Eli 17; it also says he never finished university. These details remain in the source; the confusing “You grew up / I think I did” reunion exchange has been replaced with the user-approved four lines in `ADAPTATIONS.md`. The family artifact includes the university reference; the memory and final classroom follow the supplied ages. Production should resolve those conflicts with the author before casting or making date-stamped assets.

## Verification

With Node 20+:

```sh
npm test
```

Thirty-nine automated checks cover the full story graph, source wording plus documented approved revisions, battery depletion/flicker thresholds, charging, inventory persistence, lock dependencies, cheats, voice routing, collision/substeps, navigation through gaps, trigger cancellation, actual PNG assets, every non-silent WAV and subtitle duration, and speech pause/resume/stale-load cancellation, witnessed versus blind hiding, chase persistence, difficulty migration, and camera sequence completion/cancellation. Five complete simulations have been run, one per preset. Each also audits physical key/tool access with gates closed. Repeat another preset with `AFTER_HOURS_PRESET=hard node tests/simulation.mjs`. The simulation additionally checks all checkpoint anchors, perception, capture recovery, authored Mara rig and animation, the five-finger torch grip, sprint exhaustion/recovery, and photo inspection. The end-to-end simulation instantiates the **actual Three.js school and gameplay modules**, walks navigable routes using player input, aims at real interaction targets, hides, survives both encounters, reaches the companion door, returns for Mara and completes the ending. Only the DOM/canvas UI and audio output are stubbed. It does not skip stages with debug events.

Browser automation failed to launch in the build environment (both Chrome and the in-app browser runtime), so WebGL rendering, subjective visual quality, speaker playback and mouse capture have **not** been verified in a live browser. Perform that pass before presenting this as a production slice. The game handles unsupported WebGL with an error panel and provides drag/arrow look if pointer lock is denied.

For browser inspection, append `?test=1` to the URL. This explicitly enables `window.__test` with snapshots, teleport, use, restart and accelerated dialogue tools. The F2 cheat panel works in normal play; the separate `window.__test` API is exposed only in test mode. Story progression and save recovery are designed to remain usable even when optional art/audio assets are replaced.

## Brief cutscenes and jumpscares

`src/data/cinematics.js` defines the Teacher arrival, fire memory, reunion framing, final exterior, and capture shots. `CinematicSystem` owns the camera briefly, adds letterbox bars, and returns control after completion, skip or cancellation. Trigger a shot with `{type:'cinematic', id:'reunion'}` in a beat. Add a new definition with `duration`, an actor `target`, `fov`, and optional `cue`, `shake` or `lift`. Space skips story shots after a short initial moment. Capture shots cannot be skipped. Pausing freezes camera time. Checkpoint restore cancels pending camera work before rebuilding the story.

The single authored arrival jumpscare occurs after the source's argument memory. It uses Mrs Vale's model, a door impact and a brief lighting pulse. Capture uses the same character for a close failure shot. The later user-requested room ambushes use three separate shadow variants and capture shots; all encounters share the original ending. The first-person view uses separate authored left/right skinned hand GLBs, anatomical finger chains and an opposing thumb. The right hand holds a physically sized flashlight, while the left stays relaxed. Pose and mount changes live in `world/hand-rig.js` and `world/viewmodel.js`; the lens/muzzle anchor remains attached to the held flashlight.

**Additional controls:** Hold E while facing the warped east-wing door to force it open. Press R on the failure screen to retry. Space skips a story cutscene after its first short moment; the capture shot finishes before retry becomes available.

## Searchable storage and room ambushes (v5)

Thirty storage locations provide five candidate positions for each required item. E opens/closes a real locker door or drawer; contents become selectable only after it has mostly opened. Keys and tools have no glow or remote label. Spare batteries occupy different slots from the required item in each preset. Open containers, collected contents and cleared hazards persist in checkpoints. Empty drawers contain ordinary stationery. Room-level objectives give a search area without identifying the occupied container.

Add a storage entry with `room`, `kind` (`locker`/`drawer`), rotation, and five `[x,z]` slots. Rotation points the local +Z front into the room. Keep its `approach` (1.48m in front) clear of desks and chairs. `addPickups` creates its visual cavity and collision frame; `animateStorage` moves its front and tray. Inventory places the pickup in that tray, updates its world-space focus point, and forbids collection while closed. New supplies can use `BATTERY_STORES` or the same tray association. Preserve IDs to keep saves compatible.

Anonymous shadow ambushes occupy the office, Classroom 08 and staff archive during exploration. They grab immediately, with no advance sound or warning message. When grabbed, tap and release E: holding/autorepeat does not count. Normal requires 16 taps in 6.5 seconds, Hard 22 in 6 seconds, Nightmare 26 in 5.7 seconds. Failure uses the monster's own capture shot and retries the current checkpoint. Success clears that room and saves it. Story mode disables Teacher captures only: room monsters still kill on timeout. Grabs cost 14 sanity immediately and drain 8 per second until escape. Zero sanity worsens the existing effects but does not prevent a successful escape. F2 has a separate **Disable room ambushes** cheat; **Cannot be caught** also prevents lethal timeout.

Add room definitions in `src/data/ambushes.js` using a unique ID, allowed story stages, `[minX,maxX,minZ,maxZ]` bounds, and an audio origin. `AmbushSystem` suppresses encounters during dialogue, reading, active story effects, Teacher pursuit, hiding and emotional stages. The struggle pauses walking, looking, ordinary interaction and story progression; Escape/F2 still work. Pause freezes its timer. Tune preset `taps`/`seconds`, plus live `monsterSanityDrain` and `struggleWindow` fields in the Director panel.

Historically, v5 supplied all 57 spoken assignments using level-matched Microsoft takes (53 unique WAVs); v11 replaces that set. V5 used a separate memory Eli voice, clean child Mara, older Mara, and an unhurried Teacher without the previous 18% slowdown. Device modulation remains exclusive to Mara's intercom/voicemail. Three clarity revisions are listed in ADAPTATIONS.md. These remain synthetic voice placeholders; the nonverbal laugh and actor performances are documented replacement tasks.

## Audio, settings and movement (v6)

SPACE is now jump. E remains interaction and becomes the repeated escape input only while grabbed. Q advances dialogue; SPACE still skips a skippable cinematic. Holding SPACE never produces repeated jumps. Jumping is unavailable while hiding, reading, seated, grabbed or during a shot. The player uses a height-aware body with gravity, horizontal substeps, landing/head-contact sweeps and stable support on reachable furniture. Desks, chairs and other tables are solid. Jumping can clear a low tabletop and land on it; walking off falls to the floor. Full-height walls and closed puzzle doors remain impassable. Footsteps stop in the air; landing creates sound and enemy-hearing noise. Hiding uses its explicit entry action rather than walking through the tabletop. `gravity`, `jumpSpeed`, `eyeHeight`, `crouchHeight` and `playerRadius` are in config; gravity and jump impulse are also in the Director editor.

Open **Settings** from the title or pause menu. Master, dialogue, effects, ambience, music and jumpscare sound have independent sliders. Intercom/voicemail each have gain and robotic-effect controls. Camera shake, scare-light pulse, FOV and mouse sensitivity are configurable. These preferences save under `after-hours-settings`, separately from difficulty and Director tuning. Test Intercom/Test Scare Sound are explicit previews that do not advance the story. Back returns to the title or paused menu. All controls work before entering the school.

The PA now has a broader intelligible dry signal, strongly modulated/saturated wet signal, a short room reflection, increased gain and gentler distance attenuation. Voicemail has its own more restrained damaged-device profile. Ambience and music duck automatically during spoken clips. Child memory dialogue remains free of device effects. The source spoken words remain intact; v11 replaces the bundled takes.

Twenty-two locally bundled PCM foley/design files replace the main runtime placeholder hits. Kenney's CC0 Impact Sounds and RPG Audio provide concrete/wood steps, door opening/closing/creaks, cloth, book handling and wood/metal/soft impacts. Teacher/shadow scare, escape, warning and collapse sounds are authored layered arrangements of those recordings. Sources and original licenses are in `assets/sfx/README.md`. No weapon audio is used. Rain/hum and certain tonal cues remain generated; voices remain synthetic placeholders for actor recordings.

`SFX` maps cue IDs to one or more WAVs, level, optional rate range and category bus. Add a local asset there and call `audio.cue(id, {x,y,z})`; omitted position plays a centred effect. Sources rotate through variations, cap concurrent one-shots and disconnect after playback. `stopEffects` cancels sounds on checkpoint restore. Normal gameplay and previews use the same category mixer.

All Teacher/monster scares now include a short anticipation, lunge, reaching arms, active head/jaw and recoil, with distinct recorded-foley impact designs. `applyScarePose` layers motion after an authored base clip; `CinematicSystem` drives actor/camera timing and restores actor placement on cancellation. Room-grab animation responds to struggle progress. Settings can reduce shake and mute scare sound/flash without changing progression.

Version 6.1 makes room monsters lethal in Story mode and removes their advance warnings in every preset. Teacher encounters retain their existing Story-mode protection. Infinite sanity prevents monster sanity drain but does not remove the escape deadline; Cannot be caught and Disable room ambushes remain explicit safety cheats.

Jumpscare volume, camera shake and flashing remain adjustable; zero shake and disabled flashing are still respected. The source and arrangement process are documented in `assets/sfx/README.md`. New monstrous Teacher facial textures retain Mrs Vale's alignment/identity, with deeper sockets, gaunter skin and a restrained resting-expression blend before a capture. Exact image prompts and saved paths are in `assets/images/V13-ART.md`.

Partial blurry figures have more visible contrast in fog and a slightly larger silhouette. The first is at the rear classroom doorway edge, with a tested clear sightline on an ordinary walk into the school. Main peeks disappear at 5m, side doorway peeks at 3.8m; a witnessed glimpse needs at least 0.65 seconds. The gym peek no longer waits for a door to open after the player is already too close. Revision 5 rearms old saves. **F2 → View Vanishing Figure** explicitly restores the Locker checkpoint and faces the west doorway for an immediate demonstration; walk toward it to watch the retreat. The demo is a checkpoint cheat and changes story progress to that checkpoint.

`data/environment-sounds.js` holds sparse sound origins/cues. `EnvironmentSoundSystem` chooses nearby empty-room footsteps and locker opening/creaks, avoids consecutive repeats, freezes while paused and yields to dialogue, memory scenes, pursuit, room grabs and emotional sequences. Add another cue/origin/radius to this data array to extend the layer. These sounds are independent of monster appearances and provide no attack warning. Nearby anonymous locker leaves crack open with the sound, including their vents/handles/labels; moving leaves have temporary collision bounds and reset on checkpoint changes or friendly-school transitions. Story, hiding and inventory lockers are excluded. **Ambience volume** controls this layer.

Automated geometry/state/cue checks and both full story routes verify behavior; live GPU appearance and subjective listening remain unverified in this environment.


## V14 — jointed human hands and fleeting 3D outlines

Load `http://127.0.0.1:4173/?v=14`; the title shows **V14**. Reload an already open tab to replace its loaded modules. The existing **F2 → View Vanishing Figure** demonstration restores the Locker checkpoint and faces the first doorway; it changes story progress to that checkpoint.

The old tube-built hand geometry is replaced by two independently authored, continuous skinned human hand meshes from the Immersive Web input-profile asset collection. Each side has 25 joints. Thumb opposition and MCP/PIP/DIP flexion form the right-hand power grip; the left hand has a separate relaxed pose and its own thumb orientation. Bones preserve segment lengths and use positive scales. The flashlight's 35mm rubber grip sits between the curled fingers and thumb, with the beam origin attached to its lens. The photographic skin material, nails, sleeves and modest movement sway are retained. These are authored human hand models, not photogrammetry scans or final production character art. Anatomy references, exact model sources and MIT attribution are in `assets/models/HAND-RESEARCH.md` and `HAND-LICENSE.txt`.

Doorway apparitions now consist entirely of volumetric head/body/limb geometry, with no image map, sprite or camera-facing plane. Two fixed world clipping planes expose only an 11.5cm strip behind the doorway edge. The figure keeps its world orientation and moves behind that edge during retreat. It has no facial details to inspect. Main corridor peeks vanish at 7m; the constrained side-door peeks vanish at 3.8m. A stationary observer gets at most 1.9 seconds of cumulative visible time before retreat. After at least 0.65 seconds of observation, a glimpse is saved as witnessed; interrupted shorter glimpses rearm. Revision 6 rearms figures in older saves. Room ambushes and the Teacher retain their separate behavior.

`SchoolRenderer` renders the actual apparition geometry on a dedicated object-ID/depth layer, then softens that portion of the rendered scene. Its depth comparison respects walls and door leaves. The blur is applied while the figure is visible even with the optional school lens effects disabled, using an unsigned-byte target on devices without float render targets. Camera layers, fog, background, clear color and override material are restored after the mask pass, including render failures. Other scene objects and UI stay outside the figure blur.

Tune `APPARITION_TUNING` in `src/data/hauntings.js`: `blurPixels`, `visibleStrip`, `edgeInset`, `maxGaze`, `retreatDistance` and `retreatSeconds`. Individual events can override `maxGaze`, disappearance/reveal distances, witnessed duration, door requirement and allowed stages. Edit hand mounts, sleeve dimensions and flashlight geometry in `world/viewmodel.js`; finger flexion and opposing-thumb target are in `world/hand-rig.js`. Replacement GLBs should preserve the WebXR joint names or adapt that mapping.

V14 validation: 79 automated checks, including skinned mesh weights/finite vertices, handedness, independent skeletons, bone lengths, grip clearance, animation drift, masked blur/fallback lifecycle and timed stationary-observer retreat. See `TEST-REPORT.md` for full route results and the live-rendering limitation.

## V15 — clearer encounters and flashlight grip

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173/?v=15` and reload any already open game tab. Ambient locker doors now open 66 degrees, hold, and close over 4.1 seconds, revealing actual hollow interiors. Their latch/hinge/closing sound and the five-step empty-room cue are mono positional recordings on the effects bus with less distance attenuation. Player footsteps are also louder; existing category/master volume controls still apply.

Apparitions expose a 24 cm strip that includes most of the head, use a light 3-pixel blur and stronger emissive contrast, and remain visible for up to 4.2 seconds of gaze. Corridor disappearance is now at 4.5 m, side-door disappearance at 2.2 m, and approach retreat requires at least 1.1 seconds of observation. Near arrivals can reveal a figure instead of silently missing its trigger window. The visibility ray targets actual unclipped head geometry. Haunting revision 7 rearms older saved glimpses.

Office, phone and archive room monsters each have their own encounter-relative animation and sound: alternating snatches/rocking, a receiver-like hand pose with neck snaps, and heavy two-handed raking respectively. Voices stop on encounter cleanup. Ambush revision 9 rearms these performances in older saves. The right hand now holds the flashlight along the camera's forward axis with a straighter wrist, slightly higher placement and a slimmer rubber grip. The authored hand skeleton and finger contact remain stable during movement.

V15 validation: 82 automated checks pass, including clipped-head visibility, real door occlusion, room-specific poses/audio files, wide locker opening/hold, flashlight aim and existing grip/deformation checks. Live GPU rendering and subjective audio playback remain unverified because browser automation could not start in this session.

## V19 — fleeting figures, sanity recovery and optional secret caches

Load `http://127.0.0.1:4173/?v=19`. Corridor figures retreat at 10 m, side-door peeks at 4.8 m, and gaze time is capped at 1.65 seconds. The partial-face clipping and custom sound cues remain. Haunting revision 10 rearms older saved peeks.

Stamina remains finite: zero blocks sprinting and walking/resting slowly restores the bar. After exhaustion it must recover above 40% before sprinting unlocks; that state now also clears while standing still. No faster or infinite-stamina behavior was added.

Portable grounding kits restore 25 sanity with H, clamp at 100, and save their carried count. One is inside reception's first-aid box; two more are in the new optional caches. Grounding cards in reception and the lost-property room allow repeatable recovery at 3 sanity/second after E while nearby, still, safely lit and out of danger. Moving, darkness or danger interrupts resting.

The west wall of Classroom 04 has a loose LOST PROPERTY panel at (-15, -23.6). A chest behind it contains a brass service key and grounding kit. That key opens the SERVICE panel opposite the maintenance fire-record table at (20, -52.5). Behind it, a wooden crate holds a locked service toolbox, containing spare bolt cutters, a battery and a grounding kit. The same service key unlocks the toolbox. Both rooms have actual floors/walls/passages and persistent discovery state; nested lids gate their contents. Existing required story item locations remain intact. Navigation covers the new rooms and passes beneath their door lintels.

Validation: 90 automated checks pass, and the full Normal story simulation reaches the original ending with zero captures and no progression soft locks. Live WebGL appearance remains unverified.
